To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Dscam genes of the Drosophilidae, Anopheles, and Apis are organized in a manner similar to the D. melanogaster Dscam gene, and that the alternative exons of the different species are more similar in sequence than would be expected by chance.

the Down syndrome cell adhesin molecule (Dscams) of Drosophila, Anopheles, and Apis contain numerous alternative exons that have arisen via reiteration and that the expression of these genes is likely important for the development of the nervous system in each of these organisms.
the Dscam genes of three Drosophila species, the mosquito, and the honey bee all contain a large repertoire of alternative exons that can potentially generate thousands of different isoforms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evolution of a family of genes that encode a large number of different proteins.
the evolution of the Dscamer gene and its role in insect nervous system development.
the molecular evolution of Dscam genes and the evolution of alternative splicing in insects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Dscam genes in these species have been shaped by a combination of exon duplication, exon deletion, and exon shuffling events.
the Dscam genes in the insects are highly similar in terms of the number and position of the alternative exonic sequences, but the amino acid sequence and the function of each isoform is different.
the Dscam genes in the insects studied have been subjected to strong evolutionary forces to increase the number of isoforms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Dscam genes of dipterans and hymenopters are highly conserved, and the alternative exons are more similar to the corresponding alternative exon within the same species than to the alternative exon of the other species.

the Dscam genes in insects are evolving rapidly and that the evolution of the alternative exonic sequences has occurred in a manner that preserves the ability of the gene to generate a large number of isoforms.
the insect Dscam gene family arose from a single ancestral gene by the reiterative addition of new exons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the evolution of the Dscammunity has been driven by the expansion and contraction of the number of variable exons and the duplication and deletion of the alternative exon sequences.
the Dscam genes of dipteran and hypenopteran species have evolved by a process similar to that of the Drosophilid species.
Dscam is an example of an ancient gene that has been extensively modified by reiterative duplications and deletions to generate a large repertoire of isoforms in different insect species.
